messages:
oncall-bot: PAGER - High error rate from serving fleet in us-west-2 (automated detection). Paging @jordan as primary SRE oncall. Service: inference-api. Impact: 25% 5xx spike, multiple container crashes reported.

jordan: Acked. Investigating now. Any recent deploys?

infra-bot: Deploys: none in last 30m. Autoscaler: active.

jordan: Seeing repeated CUDA driver resets on a subset of nodes, lots of `Xid 79` in `dmesg`. Suspect GPU reset cascade.

sam: Copying logs from a crashed container:```
2026-03-15T18:22:01Z serving[pid=4234]: CUDA error 700: device-side assert triggered
2026-03-15T18:22:01Z runtime: GPU reset detected, killing process
```

maya: Net team here. We're seeing ECMP path flips and transient packet reordering on IB fabric between racks 3/4 and 5. IB counters show bursts of out-of-order packets and retransmits on path to rack3-n*.

jordan: That aligns. When RDMA reorder gets severe, the serving runtime stalls waiting on KV cache fetches and task timeouts lead to container restarts. Reproducing: heavy tail latency on kvcache fetch RPCs.

chris: Any single node or multi-node?

sam: Multi-node but concentrated on a few GPU hosts: n-34, n-37, n-45. Node flaps (net) then CUDA resets cascade within the container.

jordan: First mitigation: divert traffic off affected nodes, put them into drain mode and scale up healthy pool. Taking `n-34,n-37,n-45` OOS now.

maya: Agree. I'm pushing emergency route pinning to avoid the bad ECMP paths. Will update switch fabric to prefer path via spine-2 and avoid spine-3 for these racks. ETA ~5m.

rachel: CS here - which customers are impacted? Any Dedicated customers on those racks? Need to notify affected accounts if SLOs will be breached.

jordan: Preliminary: two mid-market Dedicated pools had ~18% requests hitting the affected racks, causing 5xxs for ~12 minutes. Pulling audit now to list tenants.

infra-bot: Audit: tenant IDs impacted: T-3071, T-998, T-2210. All are on multi-tenant hosted pools except T-998 which has reserved capacity but was partially pinned to these hosts.

rachel: I'll draft a short blurb for support and account teams: "Intermittent networking issue in us-west-2 causing increased errors for a subset of requests; mitigation in progress. We'll update in 30 minutes or when we have a root cause."

jordan: While net changes propagate, applying these runtime mitigations: 1) reduce kernel `netdev_max_backlog` to limit reorder window on offending NICs, 2) disable RDMA GDR (GPU direct) on affected hosts to force fallback path, 3) increase RPC timeouts and enable fast-failover to alternate replicas.

sam: Commands I'm running on n-37 (dry-run):```bash
ssh root@n-37
echo 3000 > /proc/sys/net/core/netdev_max_backlog
# disable gdr for mlx5
modprobe -r nv_peer_mem || true
systemctl restart rdma-ndd || true
```

maya: Heads up: unloading `nv_peer_mem` will drop active RDMA connections, which is intended. Net change applied to TORs to prefer spine-2; we should see fewer retransmits in ~2-3 min.

jordan: Draining: `kubectl drain gpu-pool-node-37 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` then cordon. After drain I'll trigger a rolling restart of the serving pods on healthy nodes to rebalance KV cache warmups.

chris: Any chance to route traffic to another region for the most affected tenants as a temporary fallback?

jordan: For multi-tenant, easiest is to shift traffic to standby pool in us-east-1 for critical tenants T-998 (reserved capacity) we can failover to their dedicated standby. I'll coordinate with infra automation.

infra-bot: Failover request queued: playbook `regional-failover` triggered for T-998. Estimated 10m to shift traffic.

rachel: Notifying account teams for T-998 and T-3071 now. Will post update in #customer-impact.

maya: Link-level counters show ECN marking spikes on spine-3 for flows to racks 3/4. I've escalated to switch vendor (Mellanox support) with packet captures. They've opened case SR-20260315-77.

sam: Observed one pod crash - grabbing a core dump. `gdb` pointed to NV driver context switch during memcpy leading to GPU assert. Might be driver exposing hardware reordering issues under RDMA stress.

jordan: Current status: traffic diverted, affected nodes drained, RDMA GDR disabled on drained hosts, spine route tweak in progress, customer notifications sent. Errors down from 25% to ~4% in the last 6m. We'll stay on pager for 60m and regroup after vendor feedback.

oncall-bot: Handoff: @jordan -> @maya in 18m for next shift. Please confirm acceptance.

maya: I accept. I'll own the vendor coordination and fabric stabilization. If we still see packet reorders after config changes, plan B is temporary rack-level isolation and longer-term switch firmware patch.

jordan: Thanks team. Documenting post-incident actions: collect packet captures, export `dmesg` + driver logs from affected hosts, preserve core dumps, and run driver-version A/B test on a staging rack.

rachel: I'll prepare a customer update to go out once we have RCA.

chris: Adding follow-ups to backlog: 1) Make kvcache more tolerant to transient reorder, 2) automated redirection when IB retransmit rate > threshold, 3) hardening playbook for RDMA driver issues.

jordan: Closing initial page: mitigations effective, oncall handoff to @maya. Will reopen if errors rise above 5% or customer impact expands. :white_check_mark:
